title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is laying the point-set foundations for 'espaces stratifiés' (1981-82, the period of the Esquisse's tame-topology programme). On the previous page he set up the adjunction between spaces and preorders: specialization preorder one way, Alexandrov topology the other, with downward-closed sets closed and the closure of {i} equal to I_{<=i}. He then treated a partition X = ⊔ X_i^* as a map φ: X → I. φ is continuous iff each X_i := X_{<=i} = ⋃_{j<=i} X_j^* is closed, given local finiteness.

On this page he asks when the partition determines the preorder on I and when it is a genuine stratification. Throughout φ is continuous, I is preordered and the partition is locally finite.

- 1° The topology of I is the quotient topology: X_J^* closed ⇒ J closed, equivalently X_U^* open ⇒ U open.
- 3° The closure of each stratum is a union of strata: closure(X_j^*) = ⋃_{i<=j} X_i^*. This is the frontier condition. He shows it is equivalent to φ being an open map, via φ^{-1}(closure J) = closure(φ^{-1}J).
- 4° φ is surjective, i.e. no stratum is empty. The margin notes that 3° plus surjectivity gives 1° (a surjective open continuous map is a quotient map).
- Under 1° and 3°, the order on I is recovered as inclusion of stratum closures.

Reformulation: a datum satisfying 1° and 3° is the same as a locally finite open equivalence relation on X. I is then the quotient space, carrying its specialization preorder. I is a poset (T0) iff the strata (fibres) are locally closed.

In the ordered case he proves an equivalence: 'partitions stratifiantes' correspond to 'stratifications strictes'. A strict stratification is a locally finite family (X_i)_{i∈I} indexed by a poset I such that:
- 1° the X_i are an increasing family of closed sets covering X;
- 2° X_i ∩ X_j = ⋃_{k<=i, k<=j} X_k (the meet condition);
- 3° each X_i^* is nonempty (he calls this 'fidélité');
- 4° for j<i, X_j is nowhere dense ('rare') in X_i. This is the density condition, equivalent to closure(X_i^*) = X_i.
The passage between the two is X_i^* = X_i \ ⋃_{j<i} X_j. He names 1°+2° a 'stratification', and 1°–4° a 'strict' (faithful and dense) stratification.

The second half restates the equivalences a)⇔b)⇔c):
- a) the closure of each stratum is saturated;
- b) there is a preorder on I with closure(X_i^*) = ⋃_{j<=i} X_j^* (the order is then unique);
- c) φ is open for the quotient topology.

There is also a forward-looking remark about tame ('modérée') topology. For every partition into tame locally closed pieces one should find a smallest (coarsest) stratification, or strict stratification, compatible with it. The next page goes on to stability under pullback, local stratifications forming a presheaf, and when 'X_J^* closed ⇒ J closed' holds.
errors: The early claim 'les X_i fermés (donc les X_i^* loc. fermés)' is too quick for a genuine preorder. Continuity only makes X_{<=i} ∩ X_{>=i} locally closed, and that is the preimage of the whole equivalence class of i, not of {i}. This matches his own later statement that I is ordered iff the fibres are locally closed; the early remark only holds when I is a poset.
Statement 3° as written ('closure X_j^* = ⋃_{j<=i} X_j^*') has its indices garbled; it should read ⋃_{i<=j} X_i^*.
The meet condition is written with k ∈ i∩j; this means k ∈ closure{i} ∩ closure{j}, i.e. k<=i and k<=j.

Local finiteness is used tacitly in several places (closedness of ⋃_{j<i} X_j; a locally finite union of nowhere dense closed sets being nowhere dense). It is stated as a standing hypothesis, so this is a gap in exposition, not of substance.

Otherwise the equivalences check out: open + continuous + surjective ⇒ quotient; frontier condition ⇔ φ open; locally closed strata ⇔ T0 quotient (given the frontier condition and local finiteness); density ⇔ closure(X_i^*) = X_i.

ideas.what: A stratification of X is a continuous map φ: X → I to a preordered/ordered set with its Alexandrov topology (strata = fibres, closed sets = down-sets).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie, Higher Algebra Appendix A.5 (c. 2012-2017); used by Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Barwick–Glasman–Haine (Exodromy), Haine, Douteau, Waas
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse d'un programme, which discusses stratified structures only informally.

ideas.what: The frontier condition (closure of a stratum is a union of strata) is equivalent to the stratifying map φ: X → I being open. Then, if surjective, φ is a quotient map and the order is recovered as inclusion of stratum closures.
ideas.modern_name: frontier condition ⇔ open stratification map; poset as specialization order of the T0 quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; the openness reformulation is occasionally remarked in recent stratified homotopy theory (unsure of a precise first source)

ideas.what: Stratifications with the frontier condition are the same as locally finite open equivalence relations. The quotient is an Alexandrov space whose specialization preorder is the index preorder; it is T0 (a poset) iff the strata are locally closed.
ideas.modern_name: stratification as open map to a (finite) T0 / Alexandrov space

ideas.what: Equivalence between 'partitions stratifiantes' and 'stratifications strictes': increasing locally finite families of closed sets indexed by a poset, with the meet condition X_i ∩ X_j = ⋃_{k<=i,j} X_k, nonempty strata, and lower pieces nowhere dense in higher ones.
ideas.modern_name: closed filtration indexed by a poset / lattice map Down(I) → Closed(X); frontier condition + density
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in various forms (stratification-by-closed-filtration in Goresky–MacPherson, Mather); the poset-meet formulation is folklore

ideas.what: Programme: in tame ('modérée') topology, every partition into tame locally closed parts should admit a smallest (coarsest) stratification, or strict stratification, compatible with it.
ideas.modern_name: canonical/coarsest stratification compatible with a definable partition (o-minimal geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Compatible stratifications: Łojasiewicz, Hironaka, van den Dries (o-minimal). Canonical (minimal) Whitney stratifications: Mather, Teissier, and later o-minimal versions.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tame topology and dévissage of stratified structures; whether it states a coarsest-stratification claim I am unsure.

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks for the existence of a coarsest stratification (frontier condition, optionally strict) refining an arbitrary tame partition into locally closed pieces. This is purely topological, with no Whitney-type regularity. He does not prove it here.
missed.quote: Dans le cadre de la top. modérée, il faudra voir comment pour toute partition par des parties loc. fermées modérées, il existe une plus petite stratification ou ... strictes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Canonical coarsest stratifications are known for Whitney regularity. The purely frontier-condition (and density) version in o-minimal structures is rarely singled out as a canonical object, and canonicity matters for functorial exodromy/constructible-sheaf constructions. Modest interest; likely provable with standard o-minimal tools.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's pre-1990 foundations already use the now-standard definition 'stratification = continuous map to a poset with Alexandrov topology'. He also characterizes the frontier condition as openness of that map and locally closed strata as T0-ness of the quotient. This anticipates the Lurie / Ayala–Francis–Tanaka / Exodromy formalism by roughly 30 years.
missed.quote: Une donnée (X_i^*) satisfaisant 1°) et 3°) équivaut à une relation d'équiv. loc. finie et ouverte ... et I est l'espace quotient (avec la relation de préordre de spécialisation)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical credit rather than new mathematics. The formalism is usually attributed to Lurie's Higher Algebra appendix.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary point-set foundations. Historically it is interesting that Grothendieck in 1981-82 already defines stratifications as continuous maps to Alexandrov posets, and notes that the frontier condition is equivalent to openness, as in modern stratified homotopy theory. Mathematically it is routine and partly folklore.
transcription_corrections: 3°) should read: closure(X_j^*) = ⋃_{i<=j} X_i^* for all j ∈ I, i.e. φ is open.
'X_i ∩ X_j = ⋃_{k∈i∩j} X_k' should be ⋃_{k ∈ \bar{i} ∩ \bar{j}} X_k (k<=i and k<=j).
'(les X_i sont loc. fermés)' in the T0 criterion refers to the strata X_i^* (fibres), not the closed X_i.

The opening line reads: 'Conditions plus fortes : (conditions sur) l'application (surjective) φ est ouverte ⇔ φ^{-1}(\bar J) = \overline{φ^{-1}(J)}', with the earlier struck phrase about the quotient topology.
Margin next to the strict-stratification equivalence reads 'car I ordonné'; the margin near 3° reads 'si φ surj. ⇑', meaning 3° (with surjectivity) implies 1°.
'familles (à iso près) finies et ouvertes' belongs to the phrase 'relations d'équiv. loc. finies, à fibres loc. fermées, et ouvertes'.
